rows.noOracleRationale: DWG is a proprietary, undocumented format. The only independent implementation of any weight is LibreDWG, which is GPL-3.0 C: linking it would put a copyleft C library on this repository's test host, and no owner ruling permits that. No permissively licensed Rust DWG reader exists at all — `dxf` 0.6, the crate registered for the sibling 🖊️dxf artifact, reads DXF (the PUBLISHED interchange format Autodesk documents) and explicitly not DWG. Confidence instead comes from specification vectors and the metamorphic laws, exercised against a real 148,638-byte committed architectural drawing by an independently hand-written reader/writer of the one part of DWG that IS publicly specified: the plain preamble every file since R13 begins with — six ASCII version characters at 0x00-0x05, the `maint_version` byte at 0x12, and the little-endian `codepage` u16 at 0x13-0x14, the offsets LibreDWG's own `header.spec` documents and this subset's `DwgSnapshot` doc comments already cite (and which the real fixture confirms: 0x02 and 30/ANSI_1252). That reader never calls this repository's own 12,000-line R2004+ decoder. The narrowness is real and is stated rather than hidden: everything after the preamble is the R2004+ section map — compressed, checksummed and section-encrypted — which nothing in this repository or in the permissively licensed Rust ecosystem can regenerate, so it is carried through unchanged and the projection covers the preamble triple plus the document length only. `byteLength` is what keeps `set-snapshot` (a whole-document replacement) distinguishable from `set-version-info` (a field set in place) rather than the two collapsing into one indistinguishable edit.

rows.noOracleRationale: Two independent reasons, and the first is the decisive one. (1) NO CANDIDATE CAN SEE THE AXES. This vocabulary addresses the SOF marker byte, the frame's sample precision, whether a DAC arithmetic-conditioning segment is present, the per-class Huffman table count and each component's sampling factors — every one of them a field of the frame header or the entropy-coding mode. `image` 0.25 is registered by the sibling ✳️any subset and is the right reference for a JPEG raster, but its public API hands back pixels, dimensions and a colour type; it exposes no frame header, no SOFn discriminant, no DAC flag and no DHT view, and it offers no way to WRITE any of them either. `jpeg-decoder` exposes only an `ImageInfo`. A reference that cannot express the mutation cannot adjudicate it, and registering one anyway to satisfy the workflow would be selecting a weak oracle mechanically. (2) EVEN A PERFECT ORACLE WOULD BE MEASURING NOTHING AT THE BYTE LEVEL, because this repository's own `encode_jpg` writes a conforming baseline file and no other kind of JPEG at all: it emits `FF C0` for the frame marker, precision 8, a fixed three-component 4:2:0 sampling array, exactly four DHT segments and never a DAC — so every axis this vocabulary moves is normalized away on re-serialization. That is a real, documented property of the codec (stated in the vocabulary's own module docstring), not a gap. The substitutes are therefore the standard's own tables — ITU-T T.81 Table B.1 for the SOFn marker codes, §4.2 for the 8-bit precision mandate, Annex F for Huffman-only entropy coding, §B.2.4.2 for the four-table-per-class ceiling and §B.2.2 for the 1..=4 sampling factors — read against `check_baseline_conformance`, which is where the class verdict actually lives; plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property over the decoded snapshot. `mutate-jpg-jfif-1-01-baseline` measures the vocabulary there and says in as many words that it makes no byte-level claim, except in `identity-round-trip`, which does re-encode and reads both sides through the INDEPENDENT `image` reader the ✳️any subset registers.

rows.oracleRationale: Chosen over `serde_json` specifically BECAUSE it is independent: `serde_json` is already a genuine production runtime dependency of this repository (workspace-level `serde_json = "1.0.149"`), and this subset's own production code (`../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🦀️component.rs`) declares `impl From<serde_json::Value> for JsonValue` / the reverse conversion — a public interop path FROM the reference's own type INTO this subset's model. A `serde_json` differential would therefore be judged by something the subject already knows how to convert from, not an independent implementation. `json` (json-rust) has no such relationship: it is a standalone recursive-descent RFC 8259 parser/serializer with its own `JsonValue`/`Object`/`Number` types unrelated to this codebase, reachable from no production file. Two real gaps versus `serde_json` (and versus this subset's own codec) are absorbed rather than hidden: `json::object::Object` stores entries in a hash-ordered binary tree keyed by an FNV-1a hash of each key (see its own source), not insertion order — RFC 8259 §4 already declares object member order insignificant, so this is covered by the SAME `ordered-json-v1` core profile (array order significant, key order never) a `serde_json` oracle would also have needed; and `json::number::Number` is a `(sign, mantissa: u64, exponent: i16)` decimal pair, not this subset's own arbitrary-precision LEXEME (RFC 8259 §6 permits arbitrary precision) — numbers are compared by parsed `f64` value, a real information-loss boundary beyond IEEE-754 double precision that the real committed fixture never crosses (verified: no number token in it exceeds 3 integer digits before any decimal point). WORKED_AROUND_DEFECT: both directions of that `Number` conversion are lossy in 0.12, and neither is a precision boundary of the format -- they move values that ARE representable as `f64`. `impl From<f64> for JsonValue` rounds INTO the decimal pair (`2.7000102824824506` dumps as `...507`, `-8.881784197001252e-16` as `...253e-16`; 2 of 9 probed values moved), and `as_f64()` rounds back OUT of it by recomputing `mantissa * 10^exponent` in floating point (the fixture's `-1.3283902924697095e-17` surface normal reads out as `...097e-17`). Both were reproduced standalone against the crate alone before being worked around, and neither is hidden: the crate's PARSER and its `dump()` are exact on every probed value, so the oracle module reaches the same `Number` through those halves -- `json::parse` of the value formatted with Rust's own shortest round-trip `{:?}` going in, `value.dump().parse::<f64>()` coming out -- and pins both the defect and the fix in its own unit tests, so a later release that fixes the conversion makes those tests fail and the workaround can go. Left unfixed, the drift is one ULP per cycle and it fails the inverse law on a defect that is not this repository's.

RFC 7493 I-JSON is a restriction of the JSON VALUE SPACE, so the reference has to be a codec that (a) reads and writes RFC 8259 text and (b) surfaces the three facts the profile turns on — the ORDERED member list of every object including duplicate names, the exact number LEXEME, and the decoded string — none of which a codec that eagerly normalizes into a hash map can report. `simplejson` does all three: `object_pairs_hook` hands back `[(name, value), ...]` in document order with duplicates intact (a `dict`-producing parser silently collapses them, which would make RFC 7493 §2.3 unobservable), `parse_int`/`parse_float` hand back the raw lexeme so §2.2's ±(2^53−1) bound is checked on the digits rather than through a lossy double, and it re-serializes, so every one of this subset's ten kinds is genuinely DIFFERENTIAL rather than merely read-back. It is deliberately not CPython's stdlib `json`: that module is registrable only as the package name `json`, which the platform's own production-purity probe would then match against every `import json` in the repository, and a probe that cannot distinguish a reference library from the language's standard library is not a probe. It is deliberately not `serde_json` either: this subset's ✳️any parent declares `impl From<serde_json::Value> for JsonValue` in production, so a `serde_json` differential would compare this implementation against something it already converts from. `simplejson` has neither relationship — no file in this repository imports it, and this subset's codec has no conversion path to or from its types.

rows.noOracleRationale: `s.stdio.semio` is the ENVELOPE union over all eighteen semio subsets; there is no third-party crate that reads or writes `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, and there could not be one authoritative over a vocabulary whose eighteen wrapper variants each embed another semio-native subset's own mutation enum. What this subset OWNS is not the payload semantics — those belong to the eighteen arms and are covered by their own leaf fixtures and their own cases — but the envelope-level ROUTING: does a wrapped mutation whose arm matches the base snapshot's arm thread through, does a MISMATCHED one get refused with `mutation.target-missing` instead of silently corrupting the document, and is `set-snapshot` genuinely the only verb that can change the subset kind. Every scenario is written against exactly that, with a projection the envelope can answer without naming any arm's snapshot type: `{schema, subset, diagnostics, matchesReference}`. Confidence comes from the committed `(before, mutation, after, diff)` specification vector under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/📄set-snapshot/🧪️tests/`, already unit-tested inside the production crate, plus the routing and inverse laws as metamorphic properties. Honest limits, recorded rather than papered over: the eighteen delegating arms are exercised against each arm's OWN empty snapshot rather than a real-world document, because no real-world `.semio` artifact exists outside this repository and the committed example assets can only be decoded through `store::ArtifactDsl`/`store::ArtifactPack`, traits reached solely via a private extern-crate alias that nothing re-exports — the same structural gap wave 7 recorded for `kit`, `object`, `text` and `table`. Re-exporting those two traits would let this case read the committed `.dsl.semio` examples directly and is the single change that would most strengthen it. WAVE-14 RE-SURVEY (cross-language differential oracles, ticket 26/08/23): a second IMPLEMENTATION in another language was built for five sibling subsets in this same artifact and works end to end, so the route was re-examined here and REJECTED on two concrete, nameable blockers rather than on absence. First, the envelope's own committed documents declare the wrapped arm OPAQUE: the snapshot grammar's `document = artifact-mark subset-line REST` hands off to the arm's own grammar, the binary protocol models the wrapped pack as one opaque trailing `payload` chain, and the mutations grammar is `op = "noMutation" | tag ":" REST`. rows.noOracleRationale: Two independent reasons. (1) THE QUESTION IS NOT ONE A PACKAGE ANSWERS. This vocabulary asks whether a decoded document is inside Adobe TIFF 6.0 Part 1's Baseline class, read on five specific fields of IFD 0 — `Compression` (259) restricted to {1, 2, 32773}, `PhotometricInterpretation` (262) to 0..=3, `BitsPerSample` (258) to {1, 4, 8}, `TileWidth`/`TileLength` (322/323) absent because Baseline is strip-organized, and `StripOffsets` (273) present when it is not tiled. `image` 0.25's TIFF surface is a single-IFD raster codec: it decodes pixels and re-encodes them under its own choice of those very tags, and exposes no API to set an arbitrary compression, an out-of-range photometric or a tile-organized IFD. It could not perform any row of this vocabulary, and it holds no opinion about class membership to be compared against. (2) FOUR OF SIX KINDS ARE NOT BYTE-OBSERVABLE THROUGH THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN ENCODER EITHER: `encode_tiff` regenerates every one of `CORE_STRIP_TAGS` from the raster it is about to write, so `set-compression`, `set-photometric-interpretation`, `set-bits-per-sample` and `set-strip-offsets` are normalized away on re-serialization — a documented property of the codec, stated in the vocabulary's own module docstring, and the same constraint PNG's IHDR is under. Only the two tile kinds survive, because `TileWidth`/`TileLength` sit outside `CORE_STRIP_TAGS` and are carried verbatim. The substitutes are therefore TIFF 6.0's own tag-value tables read against `check_tiff_baseline_conformance`, which is where the class verdict lives, plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property over the decoded snapshot. `mutate-tiff-6-0-baseline` measures the vocabulary there and says in as many words that it makes no byte-level claim for those four kinds; its `identity-round-trip` does re-encode, and reads both sides through the independent IFD reader the ✳️any subset registers.

rows.noOracleRationale:
There is no credible third-party crate that is authoritative over plain-text line structure: line splitting on LF/CRLF, uniform-per-document line-ending policy and trailing-newline presence are exactly what THIS subset defines. The closest candidate, the `csv` crate already linked for the tabular subsets, genuinely helps for a NARROW part of this: with quoting disabled and a delimiter byte that cannot appear in real text, its record reader independently confirms this subset's own line-boundary splitting on single-style, NON-BLANK real content — but a standalone probe found `csv-core`'s NFA silently treats a zero-byte record as "not a record" and never emits it (confirmed unconditionally, not a `Terminator`-mode artifact), so it cannot cross-check the true line count on any real prose that has blank lines at all, which most real text does (the real fixture has 80, measured). It cannot discharge a full differential comparison either way: it collapses LF/CR/CRLF into one undifferentiated boundary and never reports which terminator it saw, so it cannot confirm or refute this subset's central claim.
